techniques.name: Slow Blues Dynamic Touch & Microtonal String Bending
techniques.description: Controlling amplifier overdrive directly from guitar volume and pick attack while executing microtonal vocal bends and thumb-over bass notes

notes: Turnaround 9th chord shapes: B9 (7-X-7-6-7-X) sliding up to C9 and C#9
Slow blues bends on frets 9, 10, and 12 of strings 1, 2, and 3
Thumb-over low B root on fret 7 of the low E string
sequence: Fret the opening sliding 9th chords on strings 5, 4, 3, and 2
Resolve cleanly to the B7 barre chord on fret 7
Execute slow-blues bends: bend up, hold with finger vibrato, and release cleanly
Roll down guitar volume to 5 for clean rhythm, roll up to 10 for screaming solo sustain
tips: Hendrix played a right-handed Fender Stratocaster strung upside-down for left-handed playing, altering string tension and pickup slant
Recorded without a bass player (Noel Redding played rhythm guitar on a Gibson Flying V), giving Hendrix total harmonic freedom
Use the neck pickup with guitar tone set to 6 for warm, woody slow-blues sustain

techniques.name: Slow 12/8 Blues Call-and-Response & Behind-the-Nut Bends
techniques.description: Balancing vocal phrases with immediate guitar answers, incorporating quarter-tone blues curls and expressive microtonal intonation

notes: Quarter-tone curl on the minor 3rd (8th fret B string or 9th fret G string) pushing toward the major 3rd
Open string sympathy: letting unpicked bass strings vibrate sympathetically under feedback
Dynamic attack: feathered thumb plucking contrasting with violent pick stabs
sequence: Listen to the vocal cadence at the end of each lyric line
Answer immediately in the two-beat pause with a descending pentatonic flourish
Apply microtonal finger vibrato at the crest of each bend
Transition into dominant ninth chord stabs on the turnaround
tips: Slow blues leaves massive space—never feel rushed to fill every beat
Use the middle finger to brace the ring finger when bending on the high strings
Keep your palm lightly brushing strings to suppress stray feedback hum

sections.name: Intro Sliding Dominant 9th Turnaround
sections.description: Hendrix's iconic opening statement featuring sliding dominant ninth chords and screaming double-stops.
notes: Slide the 9th chord shape chromatically up from B to C#
Slam the low B root with authority
Let the notes bloom into natural amplifier feedback

sections.name: Verse 1 Slow 12-Bar Blues Comping
sections.description: The slow 66 BPM 12-bar blues groove supporting Hendrix's raw storytelling vocals.
notes: Use thumb to anchor the low B on fret 7
Fill vocal pauses with short pentatonic licks
Maintain deep 12/8 slow-blues triplet pulse

sections.name: Verse 2 Vocal Call-and-Response & Fills
sections.description: Hendrix converses with his guitar, interjecting stinging blues licks between vocal statements.
notes: Leave dynamic space during vocal lines
Answer with quick blues curl on the 9th fret of the G string
Slide smoothly into the IV chord (E7)

sections.name: Main Guitar Solo (Chorus 1 - Expressive Vocal Bends)
sections.description: First chorus of the legendary slow-blues solo featuring singing, vocal-like string bends.
notes: Full-step bends on fret 10 of high E to high B root
Wring out singing, vocal finger vibrato
Dig into the pick attack for dynamic expression

sections.name: Main Guitar Solo (Chorus 2 - Screaming High Climax & Double Stops)
sections.description: The solo reaches fever pitch with high-register Albert King-style bends and stinging double stops.
notes: Push high E up a full step on fret 12
Hit double stops across strings 1 and 2 at fret 10 and fret 7
Let the amplifier feedback sing at the top of the phrase

sections.name: Outro Chromatic Turnaround & Final B9 Chord
sections.description: Descending chromatic ninth turnaround bringing the slow blues epic to a dramatic close.
notes: Slide downward from C#9 to C9 and resolve on B9
Let the final low B chord ring into rich tube saturation
Damp strings with palm to kill feedback on the final cutoff

beginner.title: 12-Bar Blues Structure in B
steps: Memorize the 12-bar blues progression: B7, E7, and F#7
Count the slow 12/8 triplet shuffle feel at 66 BPM
Strum chords on the downbeats with clean tone

intermediate.title: Sliding 9th Chords & Intro
steps: Learn the dominant ninth chord shapes (B9, C9, C#9)
Master the chromatic sliding intro turnaround
Incorporate thumb-over fretting on the low B root

advanced.title: Slow Blues Solo Mastery
steps: Master Hendrix's slow blues solo note-for-note with exact bending intonation
Control amplifier sustain and natural feedback at performance volume
Blend major and minor pentatonic vocabulary seamlessly over the 12-bar changes

commonMistakes: Rushing the slow 66 BPM tempo—slow blues demands total patience
Under-bending on the 10th fret high E string
Over-playing during vocal sections instead of leaving musical space
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Chromatic sliding 9th chord drill with metronome
5 minutes: 12-bar slow blues rhythm comping at 66 BPM
5 minutes: Slow-blues bending intonation and vibrato hold
5 minutes: Full solo playthrough with backing track
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 66 BPM with triplet subdivision clicks
Ensure downbeats land with solid, relaxed gravity
